settings.title: Settings
settings.ai_section_intro: Opt-in, read-only advice — diagnoses an error/crash log or translates config files. Never executes anything on its own. Disabled by default.
settings.ai_api_key_placeholder: Stored in the OS credential store, never in this app's database
settings.ai_diagnose_intro: Paste an error message or crash log below. The AI only reads what you paste here — it never scans your files on its own.
settings.ai_diagnose_placeholder: Paste an error or crash log here…
settings.ai_diagnosis_disclaimer: This is AI-generated advice, not a guaranteed fix — verify before acting on it.
settings.update_section_intro: Checks GitHub Releases only when you click below — nothing runs on its own. This never downloads or applies anything automatically.

legacySp.title: SP Mods · Legacy
legacySp.subtitle: Real data from list_mods (Tauri IPC → gtavmm-core). Honesty note: the database doesn't yet tag which mode/edition a mod belongs to, so this list currently shows every installed mod, not just Legacy SP ones — a real limitation, not a mockup shortcut.
legacySp.empty_body: Click "Install Mod" to install your first one, or use the CLI's `install` command.

installWizard.title: Install Mod
installWizard.pick_body_sp: Choose a mod file to install (.asi, .dll, Menyoo .xml, .zip, .7z). This targets plain single-player conventions for whichever edition (Legacy/Enhanced) is detected on this machine.
installWizard.pick_body_lspdfr: Choose a mod file to install (.asi, .dll, Menyoo .xml, .zip, .7z). This targets LSPDFR conventions — managed .dll callouts/plugins go to `Plugins\`, not SHVDN's `scripts\`.
installWizard.pick_body_fivem-client: Choose a mod file to install (.asi, .dll, Menyoo .xml, .zip, .7z). This targets the FiveM client folder set above — set that first if it's empty.
installWizard.review_note: This is a read-only preview (gtavmm-core's real `inspect` classifier) — nothing has been written yet. Conflict checking only happens once you click Install.
installWizard.protected_body: This mod would overwrite a file that's never allowed to be touched (game executables, launchers, anti-cheat). There is no override for this.
installWizard.override_body: Installing this would overwrite files owned by a different, currently-active mod. Review before overriding:
installWizard.scan_threat_body: The OS-native scanner flagged this file: {{details}}

profiles.title: Profiles
profiles.subtitle: Named sets of mods that should be active together. A mod not assigned to any profile is never touched by switching — same behavior as the CLI's `profile` command.
profiles.empty: No profiles yet — create one below.

activityLog.title: Activity Log
activityLog.subtitle: Every install, uninstall, enable, disable, and restore event, plus a local diagnostic log for internal errors.
activityLog.empty: No events match this filter yet.
activityLog.log_empty: The log file is empty or doesn't exist yet.
activityLog.auto_cleanup_notice: Auto-cleanup every 3 days. To keep the log file from growing indefinitely, its contents are automatically cleared every 3 days.
activityLog.clear_confirm_body: This permanently deletes the current contents of app.log. This cannot be undone. (The log auto-clears every 3 days anyway — this is only for clearing it early.)

savedLinks.title: Saved Links
savedLinks.subtitle: Your own bookmarked mod page URLs (e.g. gta5-mods.com) — independent of what's actually installed, so you can save one before downloading or after uninstalling.
savedLinks.empty: No saved links yet — add one above.
savedLinks.mod_setup_intro: A built-in starting-point list of prerequisite/setup tools almost every Legacy SP install needs before mods themselves go on. You can edit or remove any of these, but new links go on the My Links tab instead.
savedLinks.lspdfr_intro: A built-in starting-point list of LSPDFR/EUP mods from lcpdfr.com. You can edit or remove any of these, but new links go on the My Links tab instead.

tools.title: Tools
tools.subtitle: General-purpose utilities that aren't tied to a specific mode.
tools.editor_disclaimer: Plain-text editing only — .json / .ini / .xml. Editing .dll content is not supported here (see DLL Translation instead). Save writes directly to disk with no built-in backup — back up first if you're unsure.
tools.hash_disclaimer: Computes MD5 / SHA-1 / SHA-256 for a local file — check a downloaded mod against a known-good hash the author published.

promptLibrary.title: AI Workflow / Prompt Library
promptLibrary.intro: Your own reusable prompt text, for pasting into an AI provider by hand — not part of the AI Assistant's Action Schema, never applied or executed automatically.
promptLibrary.empty: No prompt templates yet — add one below.

modPageTools.backup_restored: Restored — extracted on top of your existing mods\ folder.
modPageTools.backup_pick_title: Select a full backup .zip to restore

dllTranslation.title: DLL Translation
dllTranslation.subtitle: AI-assisted translation of user-facing text embedded directly in a .NET (IL-only) mod DLL — direct binary patching, no source code or recompilation needed. Requires the AI assistant to be enabled with a provider first (see Settings).
dllTranslation.intro: Pick a .dll mod file. Its embedded strings will be scanned and auto-filtered to real translatable user-facing text (technical identifiers like animation names or file paths are excluded automatically).
dllTranslation.review_summary: Found {{translatable}} translatable string(s) out of {{total}} total ({{excluded}} technical string(s) excluded).
dllTranslation.edit_fields_note: Every field below is editable — type your own translation directly, or use AI to fill them all in and then adjust any of them by hand. Fields start pre-filled with the original text, so leaving one unchanged is safe.
dllTranslation.original_untouched_note: By default the translated copy is written next to the original as a new sibling file — the original is never touched. You can choose a different output location, or opt in to overwriting the original file directly instead.
dllTranslation.overwrite_original_label: Overwrite the original file instead of writing a new one
dllTranslation.overwrite_original_warning: (cannot be undone unless you have your own backup)
dllTranslation.overwrite_confirm_body: This replaces {{path}} in place with the patched version. This cannot be undone unless you have your own backup of the original file.
dllTranslation.translating: Translating and patching — this can take a while for many strings…
dllTranslation.done_summary: Done: {{translated}} string(s) translated, {{callSites}} call site(s) patched.
dllTranslation.skipped_note: {{count}} string(s) were translated but could not be located in the assembly's IL, so were skipped rather than guessed at.

fivemClient.title: FiveM · Client
fivemClient.subtitle: Client-side asset mods (textures, models) for multiplayer servers. FiveM installs per-user wherever you put it (typically under your own AppData\Local, not a shared Program Files path) — there's no reliable location to auto-detect, so this always needs to be set manually.
fivemClient.folder_placeholder: Not set — required before installing anything
fivemClient.unverified_assumption: Unverified assumption: client asset mods are assumed to reuse the same OpenIV mods\-mirroring convention as SP mods, since no real FiveM client install has been available to confirm against. Treat this workspace as the least battle-tested of the six.
fivemClient.not_wired_body: Unlike the Legacy/Enhanced pages (which reuse list_mods with a disclosed caveat), this page deliberately does not call it: installed_mod has no per-mode scoping, so showing those rows here would silently mix real GTA V game mods in with a FiveM client's own — actively misleading, not just imprecise. A real FiveM-client mod list needs either a schema change or a separate provider-scoped table before this can show real data.

enhancedSp.title: SP Mods · Enhanced
enhancedSp.subtitle: Real data from list_mods (Tauri IPC → gtavmm-core). Honesty note: same as Legacy/SP — the database doesn't yet tag which mode/edition a mod belongs to, so this is currently the exact same underlying list, just relabeled. A real per-edition split needs a schema change that hasn't been made yet.
enhancedSp.unverified_assumption: Unverified assumption: add-on vehicle/map packs are assumed to mirror Legacy's mods\update\x64\dlcpacks\ layout. Which RPF a pack's dlclist.xml entry needs internally hasn't been confirmed against a real install with RPF-inspection tooling — installs of this type should be double-checked in game. (Carried over from the EnhancedSpProvider module doc comment, not invented for this page.)
enhancedSp.empty_body: Click "Install Mod" to install your first one, or use the CLI's `install` command.

legacyLspdfr.title: LSPDFR · Legacy
legacyLspdfr.subtitle: Managed through <mono>RAGEPluginHook.exe</mono>, not the game's own launcher. Callouts and plugins install to <mono>Plugins\</mono>. Same <mono>list_mods</mono> IPC as the other workspaces — no per-mode column in the database yet, so this shows every installed mod.
legacyLspdfr.known_limitation: Known limitation: callout packs and other RAGE Plugin Hook plugins both install as a managed .dll, so this app can't yet tell them apart automatically — everything lands in Plugins\ rather than the community's Plugins\LSPDFR\ subfolder for callouts specifically. Move a callout there yourself if a pack expects it. (Confirmed against a real LSPDFR install's backup — see the provider module docs; this specific callout-subfolder nuance is the one part not yet automated, not an unverified guess about the whole convention.)

enhancedLspdfr.title: LSPDFR · Enhanced
enhancedLspdfr.subtitle: RPH's Enhanced-edition support is new (Public Preview since 2026-04) — treat everything here as more likely to need a manual fix than the Legacy equivalent. Same <mono>list_mods</mono> IPC as every other workspace — no per-mode column yet, so this shows every installed mod.
enhancedLspdfr.beta_support: Beta-grade support: this app's Enhanced LSPDFR conventions (the Plugins\ folder, add-on-pack mirroring) are carried over from the Legacy provider on the assumption they still hold — they haven't been individually re-verified against a real Enhanced RPH install. Expect rougher edges than every other page in this app; check installs in-game before trusting them.

fivemServer.title: FiveM · Server
fivemServer.subtitle: Resolves a correct load order for your <mono>resources\</mono> folder from each resource's declared <mono>fxmanifest.lua</mono> dependencies — real IPC to <mono>gtavmm-core</mono>, not a demo snapshot. Browse or type/paste a path below.
fivemServer.empty_body: Point this at your server's <mono>resources\</mono> folder, then click Resolve order.
fivemServer.apply_disclaimer: Writes only a clearly-marked, idempotent block into <mono>server.cfg</mono> — every other setting (hostname, maxclients, unrelated ensures) is left untouched; re-running updates the block in place instead of duplicating it.

fivemConverter.title: FiveM · Converter
fivemConverter.subtitle: Converts an SP add-on vehicle pack straight into a FiveM resource — reads the dlc.rpf directly (including any nested vehicles.rpf), no OpenIV/CodeWalker extraction step needed. Real IPC to gtavmm-core, not a demo snapshot. Vehicle/Add-on packs only — script mod conversion isn't built.
fivemConverter.unverified_assumption: Unverified assumption: verified end-to-end against four real SP add-on vehicle mods so far (see project notes) — including packs with carcols.meta, nested per-language localization archives, non-ASCII paths, and 16 vehicles declared in a single DLC. Still untested: a vehicles.rpf nesting a third level of archive.
fivemConverter.manifest_generated: Generated (glob-based, matches the community-standard Add-on Car template)
